column6: rationale -- scripts/gen-membudget.py; docs/SIZING.md "Memory budgets"; CONTRIBUTING.md "Memory budgets" for flipping an open row.

the groups, partitions and spill state of an aggregate scan: 81 MB held by agg_group_passes and agg_partitions_many at the default work_mem (the context of the scan 42 MB, 8.5 MB of the combo cache, which keeps up to sift.agg_combo_cache combinations, not bytes); the intended budget is hash_mem plus 8 MB
the table of a lookup join, hashed by key: 22.8 MB measured, it follows the rows of the dimension table (slope row lookup_join_label)
the inverted buffer of a CREATE INDEX of a search index, its runs and the page of text (9.5 MB held at maintenance_work_mem 1MB: 13.6 MB)
the runs and the inverted buffer of a merge of search segments
the sort of the documents of a sealed segment

the state of a search scan: each open segment holds about 165 kB (a 64 kB dictionary block, its header and stream reader), up to 128 segments (24 MB), plus 8 MB of cursors, candidates and top-N; 0.5 MB at 2 segments, 9.8 MB at 60
the walk of one segment and the heap check of sift.verify: a context for each segment, deleted at its end (before: 115 MB held for 60 segments, now 0.2 MB)
the decoded unit of the sweep of overflow records (4.7 MB)
the two sorts and the hashes of sift.col_verify (23.9 MB at the default maintenance_work_mem)
the reader of the write buffer of a column index (12.6 MB)
the directory snapshot and the steps of the ambulkdelete and amvacuumcleanup of an index (0.5 MB)

what one step of the maintenance worker holds besides its promotion or merge, once they end; not measured yet: the tests of this tree run no worker step to its end, so the ceiling is a placeholder until a worker test records a peak
the segment read of a value store usage count, reset at each segment (88 kB)
